title: Amazon Listing Suppressed for Image Issues? Troubleshooting Guide | edit-photo
heading: How to Fix Amazon Listing Image Suppression
description: Troubleshoot Amazon listing image suppression by checking the reported image issue, correcting the affected asset, and resubmitting it with a clear QA workflow.

blocks.text: When Amazon reports an image-related listing suppression, start with the exact message shown for that listing. The useful question is not how quickly any image can be replaced, but which asset failed, what Amazon says is wrong, and whether the corrected file resolves that specific issue. Review and processing times vary, and replacing an image does not guarantee reinstatement.
What image suppression means

An image-related suppression means Amazon has identified an unresolved image issue that affects the listing. It does not automatically tell you that every image is invalid or that the entire image set must be rebuilt. Use the listing status and issue details in Seller Central as the source of truth, because the affected asset, category, marketplace, and required action can differ.
Read the exact Seller Central reason

Open the affected listing and record the complete issue message before editing anything. Note the ASIN or SKU, marketplace, image role, reported problem, and any file reference or submission instruction. Do not diagnose from a generic email subject or from an older listing with a similar symptom.

items.label: Copy the reason
items.text: Keep the wording Amazon currently shows so you can compare it after resubmission.

items.label: Check the scope
items.text: Confirm whether the message names one image, the main image, another image role, or a broader listing issue.

items.label: Separate image issues
items.text: If the message concerns product data, account status, or another non-image field, changing the image alone will not address it.

blocks.text: Confirm which image is affected

Compare the image referenced in Seller Central with the files you uploaded. Check whether it is the current main image, a secondary image, or an older file still being processed. Match the product, variant, bundle, and packaging version before replacing anything. This prevents a correct image from being overwritten while the reported file remains unchanged.
If the problem is broader than one suppressed asset,
blocks.label: review the complete Amazon product image checklist

blocks.text: Main image background issues

If Amazon identifies the main-image background, inspect the actual exported file rather than the editing preview. Look for a background that is off-white, uneven, transparent when a flattened background is expected, or contaminated by shadows and retained scene pixels. Keep the detailed main-image rules in one place instead of relying on a shortened checklist here.
For current main-image background requirements and export checks,
blocks.label: use the Amazon white-background photo guide

blocks.text: When the reported problem requires a fresh white-background asset,
blocks.label: open the Amazon white background maker

blocks.text: Cropping and product framing

Check whether any product part is clipped, whether the item is too small to identify clearly, or whether props and empty space make the subject ambiguous. Do not apply a universal margin percentage. The appropriate crop depends on the product shape and Amazon's current requirements for the relevant category and marketplace. Preserve the complete product unless the current rules explicitly allow a different presentation.
Text, logos and watermark problems

Inspect the affected image for promotional text, added logos, badges, borders, watermarks, or graphics that conflict with the reported requirement. If a supplier file contains a watermark, obtain an authorized clean source or create your own photograph. edit-photo is not a watermark-removal or arbitrary object-removal tool.
Edge and transparency issues

Background removal can leave halos, retained background pixels, missing product parts, or accidental transparency around handles, cables, glass, mesh, and fine edges. Compare the cutout with the source at 100% zoom. Correct the mask where the product contour is wrong, then prepare the output required for the affected image role.
For a focused cutout and manual edge-inspection workflow,
blocks.label: use the product background remover

blocks.text: If you need a reusable transparent source before creating the marketplace export,
blocks.label: review the transparent PNG workflow

blocks.text: File and export checks

Open the final exported file and verify that it is the file you intend to submit. Check orientation, dimensions, format, file integrity, compression damage, transparency handling, and whether the product still matches the listing. Compare technical requirements with the current instructions in Seller Central instead of copying values from an old workflow.
Fix and resubmit

items.label: Correct only the diagnosed issue
items.text: Return to the best available source and make the smallest change that directly addresses the reported problem.

items.label: Run a final QA comparison
items.text: Compare the replacement with the source, the listing, the exact suppression message, and Amazon's current instructions.

items.label: Submit through the specified workflow
items.text: Upload or replace the affected asset in Seller Central and follow any additional action requested for that issue.

items.label: Keep a record
items.text: Save the submitted filename, submission time, issue wording, and corrected master so the next review is traceable.

blocks.text: edit-photo can remove a background, help you inspect and correct cutout edges, and prepare clean white or transparent assets for the next export step. It does not repair lighting, calibrate color automatically, remove arbitrary objects, generate A+ Content, guarantee Amazon approval, or guarantee that a listing will be reinstated.
Wait for Amazon to process the replacement

After resubmission, allow Amazon's systems to process the replacement and watch the current listing status in Seller Central. Avoid repeatedly uploading different versions before the status updates unless Amazon instructs you to do so; otherwise it becomes difficult to know which file is being reviewed. Processing time can vary, so do not treat a fixed timeline as a promise.
What to do if suppression remains

Read the current error again and compare it with the reason you originally recorded. If the message changed, investigate the new issue separately. If it did not change, confirm that the replacement reached the correct ASIN, variant, marketplace, and image role, and that no older asset is still active. Follow the support or appeal path shown in Seller Central when the file appears correct but the issue remains.
Use Amazon's current account-specific instructions when diagnosing and resubmitting:
blocks.label: Amazon Seller Central Help

items.question: Does every Amazon listing suppression require a new main image?
items.answer: No. Read the exact Seller Central reason and confirm which image or listing field is affected before replacing anything. A secondary image or a non-image issue requires a different response.

items.question: How quickly will Amazon restore a listing after an image replacement?
items.answer: Processing and review times vary. Monitor the listing status in Seller Central and follow the instructions shown for the specific issue; an image replacement does not guarantee reinstatement.

items.question: Should I upload a transparent PNG as the Amazon main image?
items.answer: Do not assume transparency and a white background are interchangeable. Follow the dedicated Amazon white-background guide and verify the current requirements for the relevant marketplace and category.

items.question: Can edit-photo fix every image-related suppression?
items.answer: No. edit-photo supports background removal, cutout-edge correction, and preparation of clean white or transparent assets. It does not repair lighting, calibrate color, remove arbitrary objects, generate A+ Content, or guarantee approval.

items.question: What should I check if the suppression remains after resubmission?
items.answer: Re-read the current error, confirm the corrected file reached the correct listing and image role, check whether the issue changed, and use the support or appeal path provided in Seller Central when needed.
